description:
Make `jit claim status` and `jit claim list` report each lease's staleness as computed when they read it, so consumers of their JSON need no stored flag.

## Background

`jit claim status` and `jit claim list` return leases from `ClaimCoordinator::get_active_leases` (`crates/jit/src/storage/claim_coordinator.rs:1188-1230`, called from `commands/claim.rs:469-535`). Each lease's `stale` field is whatever the index stored; it is computed only when the index is rebuilt from the log (`claim_coordinator.rs:1334`). `Lease::is_stale(now)` (`:105`) computes it. The human render reads the field at `main.rs:7811`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `claim status` and `claim list` report each lease's `stale` as `Lease::is_stale(now)` at the time of the read, in JSON and human output.
- [hard] REQ-02: A coordinator unit test shows that a lease whose heartbeat lapsed after it was stored is reported stale.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the semantic-types epic (2195c98f): issue ids are `IssueId`, gate-run ids `GateRunId`, gate keys `GateKey`, lease ids `LeaseId`, events are an `Event` envelope around a tagged `EventBody`, and record paths come from `VirtualPath` constructors. Line citations name current code, which that epic retypes.
title: Lease status reports staleness computed at read time
